thread:
maya: alert from cloudwatch - unusual ssh auths to staging-app1. 3 failed attempts then a success from 54.198.12.34 using deploy key 'redwood-staging-deploy'. i see a recent commit in repo infra-web that added an encrypted key file. linking logs.

sec-bot: [automated] Suspicious SSH auth detected on staging-app1 from IP 54.198.12.34. Created incident INC-2026-1123.

alex: thanks for flagging. can someone confirm where that deploy key is stored? i thought staging uses instance-profile only.

maya: looks like repo infra-web has a file tools/ci/keys/staging_key.enc added in commit 7a3c2e. the file is encrypted with a passphrase that was in GH secret STAGING_KEY_PASSPHRASE which, annoyingly, was present in org secrets and recently copied to a fork by a contractor. unsure if fork had access to run actions.

sam: ugh. i can immediately revoke the deploy key from the app host and remove the deploy keys in repo. steps:
- remove authorized_keys entry on staging-app1
- rotate any KMS-wrapped secrets that use the same key
- remove STAGING_KEY_PASSPHRASE from org secrets and force rotate

jun: i'll take host containment. running:
```
ssh root@staging-app1 'sed -n "/redwood-staging-deploy/=" && sed -n "/redwood-staging-deploy/p" /home/deploy/.ssh/authorized_keys'
# then comment out the line
```
jun: done, key entry commented, created ticket HW-987 for host ACL change.

eva: i'm on secrets rotation. which KMS key wrapped artifacts do we need to rotate? looks like the CI pipeline used aws-kms-key: arn:aws:kms:us-west-2:123456:key/abcd-ef12. i'll start a rotation for any secrets encrypted with that key and rotate IAM role creds.

alex: also block the IP at the cloud firewall for now, and open an ephemeral restriction so no external access to staging except from our CI IPs.

maya: i've opened INC-2026-1123 in pager duty, paging oncall. i've added a short timeline in the incident doc. also ran a repo scan across org for PEM headers and found 2 other matches in old branches (not merged). creating GH issues to delete those branches and revoke any associated secrets.

sam: quick note on credential revocation: if the passphrase was in an org secret and copied to a fork, that means the fork could have used actions to decrypt if workflows allowed. let's mark any PR or fork-run logs since that commit and search for actions with `secrets: STAGING_KEY_PASSPHRASE` in runs. gh api to list runs helps:
```
gh run list --repo redwood/infra-web --workflow ci.yml --json database
```

maya: found a run from contractor-fork/infra-web that executed 2026-03-07 02:14 UTC. artifacts show a `decrypt_and_deploy.sh` step.

jun: is there any sign of lateral movement? iam/cloudtrail shows an auth from the staging host to s3://redwood-backups at 02:16. i'll pull the access logs and block any iam session tokens that started at that time.

eva: rotated KMS key aliases and re-encrypted the backups snapshot. rotated service account keys used by CI. also raised a change to require KMS key usage via centralized KMS policy (no direct inline decrypts) - PR: https://github.com/redwood/internal/pull/201

alex: post-containment tasks: repo retro, tighten RBAC for org secrets (restrict to teams), add pre-receive hook to block committed key files, add scheduled scan for encrypted blobs in PRs, update onboarding docs to avoid checked-in keys. also need audit logging to retain 90d of actions for pulls and secret changes.

maya: i'm drafting the public incident note for internal comms (inc-2026-1123/notes). can we list owners for followups? proposed owners:
- repo scans and pre-receive: alex
- secret rotation policy: eva
- host + network lockdown: jun
- incident writeup + retro: maya

sam: assigned and created follow-up tickets:
- SEC-2452 pre-receive hook + enforcement
- SEC-2453 org secret RBAC tightening
- SEC-2454 audit retention increase + KMS policy
- SEC-2455 retro + dev training

sec-bot: [automated] Reminder: please attach proofs of rotation (rotation logs, KMS key rotation id, GH secrets removal) to INC-2026-1123 within 48h.

maya: uploading rotation logs and a short timeline. cc @product @support for heads-up to anyone who might have pulled staging artifacts. recommend we mark this P2 since access was to staging only and we contained quickly.

jun: final note - we've deployed a sticky rule on firewall and tightened the EC2 metadata role to deny lateral s3 access from staging instances. leaving incident open for the retro, but no active access now.

alex: good job. let's do a 30-min retro tomorrow to cover prevention and detection gaps. i'll book the slot and share notes.
